# BLO-29965 — re-assert the execution lock before `git push` / `gh pr create`

Tracking: [BLO-29965](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-29965)

**Files:** `src/server/env-guard.ts`, `src/server/env-guard.test.ts`

Two runs of one agent each opened a PR for the same issue, and one run's push
collided with the other's. The inbox-selection fix already on master
([#1742](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1742)) removes the measured
way the second run got there. It does not stop a run that never calls checkout,
or one that lost the lock partway through, from making outward side effects.

The embedded PreToolUse guard (`ENV_GUARD_SCRIPT`) now re-checks the lock when a
Bash command looks like a git push or `gh pr create`. It reads
`PAPERCLIP_TASK_ID` / `PAPERCLIP_RUN_ID` / `PAPERCLIP_API_URL` /
`PAPERCLIP_API_KEY` and makes one `GET /api/issues/:id`. It exits 2 only when the
server names a **different** run as `executionRunId`. The block message tells the
run to re-assert the lock with checkout and to stop on 409. Everything else is
allowed and makes no API call: commands that don't match, runs with no task id
(PR-review runs have none), missing credentials, an API error or a 10 s timeout,
and a lock that nobody holds. Same fail-open rule as the env-dump block.

Tests start a fake API in-process and run the real embedded script. They cover
four outward command forms being blocked, plus allow-on-own-lock, allow-on-no-lock,
fail-open-on-500, no API call for non-matching commands, and no API call without
a task id. Three mutations were checked separately, and each one turns the suite
red: removing the block, removing the command prefilter, and dropping the
`holder === run` exemption.
